newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB, Commonwealth Bank hit fresh highs.
newsitem.headline: NAB, Commonwealth Bank hit fresh highs.

text.p: Shares in Commonwealth Bank of Australia and National Australia Bank (NAB) touched record highs in Wednesday afternoon trading as investors punted that a Westpac Banking Corporation profit that bettered market expectations would be matched by others in the sector.
By 2.55 p.m. (0245 GMT), Commonwealth Bank shares were 20 cents higher at A$14.75, having hit an all time high of A$14.82 after rebounding off an intraday low of A$14.44.
Sector leader NAB was up 8.3 cents at A$18.42 after touching a record high of A$18.49 and bouncing off an intraday low of A$18.15.
Westpac announced a 12.9 percent rise in first half net profit to A$638 million and saw its shares hit an intraday high of A$7.60 before finding profit takers.
Brokers said result had been quickly absorbed by the market and reflected in pricing.
"It looks good for the rest with NAB due tomorrow. As a group, their earnings still look strong," said a Sydney broker.
Others noted the optimistic earnings outlook but were sceptical about whether the bullishness was to last.
"It's hard to pinpoint just why they are so strong," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based investment bank.
"Strong earnings have largely been priced in and NAB in particular are looking very expensive."
NAB is due to report on Thursday while ANZ Bank reports next week. Commonwealth Bank balances in June and reports later in the year.
By 3.35 p.m. (0535 GMT), NAB shares were 1.3 cents higher at A$18.35 while Commonwealth Bank shares up 18 cents at A$14.73.
ANZ Bank shares, which suffered from some switching to the largest two banks, was down seven cents at A$8.42 while Westpac shares had slipped to A$7.45, down five cents on the day.
